lessons.title: Where were you?
lessons.scenario: Smarty is in the playroom and asks Mia and Sam where they were yesterday.

items.note: Ask ‘Where were you?’ to find out where someone was in the past.
Use ‘I was’ to say where you were in the past.
Use ‘you were’ when talking to someone about where they were.

items.example: I was at the park yesterday.
items.note: Say ‘yesterday’ for the day before today.

items.example: I was at home last night.
items.note: Say ‘last night’ for the night before today.

grammar.title: was and were
grammar.explanation: Use was with I, he, she, and it. Use were with you, we, and they. Add yesterday or last night at the start or end of the sentence.
examples: You were at home last night.

practice.prompt: Smarty wants to know where Mia was. Which question does he ask?
practice.explanation: Use Where were you? to ask about a place in the past.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: I was talks about where you were in the past.

practice.prompt: Match the phrases with their meanings.

pairs.right: We were at home last night.

practice.explanation: Yesterday means the day before today, and last night means the night before today.

practice.prompt: Mia talks about herself yesterday. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use I was when talking about yourself in the past.

practice.prompt: Smarty talks to Sam about yesterday. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use you were with you.

practice.prompt: Ask your friend about last night. Build the question.
practice.explanation: Put Where were you before last night to ask the question.

practice.prompt: Say that you were in the kitchen last night. Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I was in the kitchen last night.
practice.explanation: Start with I was, then the place, then last night.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: I was at the library yesterday.
practice.answer: I was at the library yesterday.
practice.explanation: Use I was for yourself and yesterday for the day before today.

story.hook: Where were Mia, Sam, and Smarty yesterday and last night?

questions.explanation: Mia says: I was at school yesterday.

questions.explanation: Mia says: We were at home.

questions.prompt: Where was Smarty?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: I was in this room!

mission.setup: Smarty chats with you in the playroom. Tell him where you were yesterday and last night.

turns.smarty: Hello! Where were you yesterday?
turns.hint: Start with ‘I was’ and name a place like home, school, or the park.

turns.smarty: And where were you last night?
turns.example: I was at home last night.
turns.hint: Say ‘I was’ and where you were last night.

turns.smarty: Ask me where I was yesterday!

lessons.title: Was and were
lessons.canDo: Use was and were in questions and negatives
lessons.scenario: Smarty looks for his missing yellow box in the playroom and questions Ben and Lily.

items.example: I was not at school yesterday.
items.note: Add ‘not’ after ‘was’ to say where someone or something was not.

items.example: We were not at the cinema.
items.note: Add ‘not’ after ‘were’ with you, we, or they.
Start a yes-or-no question about one thing or the weather with ‘Was it?’.

items.example: Were you at home last night?
items.note: Start a yes-or-no question to someone with ‘Were you?’.

grammar.title: Questions and negatives with was/were
grammar.explanation: Put was or were before the person to ask a question (Were you at home?, Was it cold?). Put not after was or were to say no (I was not tired, We were not at school).
examples: Were you at the park yesterday?
I was not at the cinema last night.

practice.prompt: Smarty wants to ask Ben if he was at home. Which question is right?
practice.explanation: Put Were before you to ask a question.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Was it asks a question about the weather yesterday.

practice.prompt: Match the sentence halves.
practice.explanation: Use I was not for one person and We were not for more than one person.

practice.prompt: Ben was at home, not at school. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use was not after I.

practice.prompt: Lily and Mia were at home, not at the park. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: We ___ at the park last night.
practice.explanation: Use were not after we.

practice.prompt: Ask Lily if she was at the cinema. Build the question.
practice.explanation: Start the question with Were you.

practice.prompt: Ask if the weather was cold yesterday. Build the question.
practice.explanation: Start with Was it to ask about the weather in the past.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Use I was not to say how you did not feel.

mission.setup: Smarty is asking questions in the playroom. Answer him using was, were, was not, or were not.

turns.smarty: Were you at school yesterday?
turns.example: No, I was not at school.
turns.hint: Say ‘Yes, I was’ or ‘No, I was not’.

turns.smarty: Was it sunny yesterday?
turns.hint: Say ‘Yes, it was’ or ‘No, it was not’.

turns.smarty: Ask me if I was tired last night!
turns.hint: Start with ‘Were you tired…’

lessons.title: Went had saw ate
lessons.canDo: Say what you did with four common verbs
lessons.scenario: Leo and Ana sit in Smarty's playroom and talk about places they went and lunch yesterday.

items.example: I went to the park yesterday.
items.note: ‘Went’ is the past of ‘go’—use ‘I went to…’ for a place you visited.
‘Had’ is the past of ‘have’—use it for meals, drinks, or things you had.
‘Saw’ is the past of ‘see’—use it for people, animals, or things you saw.
‘Ate’ is the past of ‘eat’—use it to say what food you ate.

grammar.title: Four irregular past verbs
grammar.explanation: These four verbs change form in the past: go becomes went, have becomes had, see becomes saw, and eat becomes ate. The form stays the same for I, you, he, she, we, and they.
examples: She ate a sandwich for lunch.

practice.prompt: Match each verb today with its past form.
practice.explanation: Go becomes went, have becomes had, see becomes saw, and eat becomes ate.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: I went to the museum says where you went.

practice.prompt: Leo looked at a bird in a tree yesterday. Which sentence is right?
practice.explanation: Use I saw for something you looked at in the past.

practice.prompt: Ana talks about her snack yesterday. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use ate (the past of eat) for food.

practice.prompt: Smarty talks about his meal last night. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I ___ fish for dinner last night.
practice.explanation: Use I had for a meal like breakfast, lunch, or dinner.

practice.prompt: Say that you went to the park yesterday. Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I went to the park yesterday.
practice.explanation: Use I went to before a place.

practice.prompt: Say that you ate a sandwich for lunch. Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I ate a sandwich for lunch.
practice.explanation: Start with I ate, then the food.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: Use I saw for a person you met or looked at.

story.hook: What did Leo see at the park yesterday?

image.describe: Leo and Ana sit on a colorful rug in Smarty's playroom, showing Smarty a drawing of a blue bird and an apple.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello, Leo! Hello, Ana!

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Yesterday I went to the park.

lines.speaker: Ana

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: At the park, I saw a big blue bird in a tree!

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Nice! For lunch, I had a sandwich and I ate a red apple.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: I had fish for dinner last night. It was delicious!

questions.prompt: Where did Ana go yesterday?
questions.explanation: Ana says: I went to the museum yesterday!

questions.prompt: What did Leo see at the park?
questions.explanation: Leo says: I saw a big blue bird in a tree!

questions.prompt: What did Ana eat for lunch?
questions.explanation: Ana says: I ate a red apple.

mission.setup: Tell Smarty one place you went and what you had or ate yesterday.

turns.smarty: Yesterday I went to the kitchen. Where did you go?
turns.example: I went to the park yesterday.
turns.hint: Say ‘I went to…’ and name a place.

turns.smarty: I had fish for dinner. What did you eat yesterday?
turns.hint: Start with ‘I ate…’ or ‘I had…’ and name a food.

turns.smarty: I saw a bird outside! What did you see yesterday?
turns.hint: Say ‘I saw…’ and name a person, animal, or thing.

lessons.title: Review
lessons.scenario: Smarty hosts a fun quiz in the playroom to review where everyone was and what they did.

practice.prompt: Smarty asks Mia about yesterday. Which question is right?
practice.explanation: Use were with you: Where were you yesterday?

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: We were not at the cinema.
practice.answer: We were not at the cinema.
options: We were not at the cinema.
I was not at the cinema.
practice.explanation: Were not makes the sentence negative for we.

practice.prompt: Match the beginnings and endings.
practice.explanation: Went goes with a place, had with a drink or meal, saw with something you looked at, and ate with food.

practice.prompt: Sam stayed home last night. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I ___ at the park last night.
practice.explanation: Use was not after I.

practice.prompt: Ask your friend if they were at home. Complete the question.
practice.explanation: Start the question with Were you.

practice.prompt: Ask if the sandwich was delicious. Build the question.
practice.explanation: Use Was it to ask about one thing in the past.

practice.prompt: Say that you were at the park and you had juice. Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I was at the park and I had juice.
practice.explanation: Use I was for the place and I had for the drink.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: You were at home and I went to school.
practice.answer: You were at home and I went to school.
practice.explanation: Use you were for your friend and I went for yourself.

story.hook: What did Sam and Mia have at the park?

mission.setup: Smarty checks what you remember from Lessons 1 to 3. Answer his questions!

turns.smarty: Where were you last night?
turns.example: I was at home last night.
turns.hint: Say ‘I was…’ and where you were.

accept: ^(?:yes|no)(?: i was(?: not)?(?: at the cinema)?)?$
^i was(?: not)? at the cinema(?: yesterday)?$

turns.hint: Say ‘Yes, I was’ or ‘No, I was not’.

turns.smarty: Tell me one thing you ate or saw yesterday!

lessons.title: Played and watched
lessons.canDo: Say what you did with four more verbs
lessons.scenario: Omar and Zara join Smarty in the playroom and share what they did yesterday.

items.note: Add ‘-ed’ to ‘play’ to say ‘I played’ for sports, music, or games.
Add ‘-ed’ to ‘watch’ to say ‘I watched’ for TV or a game.
Use ‘I visited’ when you went to see a person or a place.
Use ‘I cooked’ when you made hot food in the kitchen.

grammar.title: Regular past verbs ending in -ed
grammar.explanation: Many English verbs form the past by adding -ed: play becomes played, watch becomes watched, visit becomes visited, and cook becomes cooked.

practice.prompt: Match the verbs with what goes best after them.
practice.explanation: Played goes with sports or games, watched with TV, visited with people or places, and cooked with food.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: I visited my grandmother means you went to see her.

practice.prompt: Omar made hot chicken and rice in the kitchen. Which verb fits?
practice.explanation: Use I cooked for making hot food.

practice.prompt: Zara talks about sports in the park. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use played for sports like football.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about last night.
practice.text: I ___ TV in the living room.
practice.explanation: Use watched with TV.

practice.prompt: Say that you cooked soup for dinner. Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Start with I cooked, then the food.

practice.prompt: Say that you visited the museum yesterday. Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use I visited before the place.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: We played a game last night.
practice.answer: We played a game last night.
practice.explanation: Played works for games as well as sports.

questions.prompt: What did Zara play in the park?
questions.explanation: Zara says: I played football in the park yesterday.

questions.prompt: What did Omar cook for dinner?

mission.setup: Tell Smarty what you played, watched, visited, or cooked yesterday.

turns.smarty: Yesterday I played a game. What did you play or watch?
turns.hint: Say ‘I played…’ or ‘I watched TV’.

turns.smarty: Nice! Who or where did you visit yesterday?
turns.hint: Start with ‘I visited…’ and name a person or place.

turns.smarty: What did you cook for dinner?
accept: ^i cooked (?:some )?(?:rice|soup|chicken|fish|egg)(?: for dinner)?(?: yesterday| last night)?$
turns.hint: Say ‘I cooked…’ and name a food.

lessons.title: Bought made came
lessons.scenario: Tom and Mia bring a cake and a gift to Smarty's playroom.

items.example: I bought a new hat yesterday.
items.note: ‘Bought’ is the past of ‘buy’—use it for things you paid for in a shop or market.
‘Made’ is the past of ‘make’—use it when you created or baked something.

items.example: I came home at five o'clock.
items.note: ‘Came’ is the past of ‘come’—use it when someone arrived here or came home.

items.example: I met my friend at the market.
items.note: ‘Met’ is the past of ‘meet’—use it when you saw and talked to someone.

grammar.title: Four more irregular verbs
grammar.explanation: Learn four more irregular past verbs: buy becomes bought, make becomes made, come becomes came, and meet becomes met.
examples: I bought juice at the market.

practice.prompt: Match each verb today with its past form.
practice.explanation: Buy becomes bought, make becomes made, come becomes came, and meet becomes met.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I bought some juice at the market.
practice.answer: I bought some juice at the market.
options: I bought some juice at the market.
I made some juice at the market.
I bought some bread at the market.
practice.explanation: I bought is the past of I buy.

practice.prompt: Mia baked a sweet cake in the kitchen. Which sentence is right?
practice.explanation: Use I made for something you created or baked.

practice.prompt: Mia saw Tom at the market and talked to him. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use met when you meet someone in the past.

practice.prompt: Tom arrived at Smarty's home yesterday. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Came is the past of come.

practice.prompt: Say that you bought a blue hat. Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Start with I bought, then the item you paid for.

practice.prompt: Say that you came home by bus. Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use I came home to say you arrived back at home.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: I met my best friend yesterday.
practice.answer: I met my best friend yesterday.
practice.explanation: I met is the past of I meet.

questions.explanation: Mia says: And I made this sweet cake in the kitchen!

turns.smarty: Yesterday I bought a new book. What did you buy?
turns.hint: Say ‘I bought…’ and name something you bought.

turns.hint: Say ‘I made a cake’ or ‘I made a sandwich’.

turns.smarty: Who did you meet yesterday?
turns.hint: Say ‘I met…’ and name a friend or family member.

lessons.title: Studied helped walked
lessons.canDo: Say what you did at school and outside
lessons.scenario: Smarty asks Sam and Lily about school, homework, and walking home yesterday.

items.note: ‘Studied’ is the past of ‘study’—notice the ‘y’ changes to ‘ied’.

items.example: I helped my mother at home.
items.note: Use ‘I helped’ when you did something helpful for someone.
Use ‘I walked’ when you went somewhere on foot.
Start past questions with ‘Did you’ and use the base verb, like ‘walk’ or ‘study’.

grammar.title: Past questions with Did you…?
grammar.explanation: To ask a yes-or-no question about past actions, start with Did you followed by the base verb (Did you study?, Did you walk?, Did you help?). Notice that after Did, the verb does not have -ed.
examples: Did you walk in the park?

practice.prompt: Smarty asks Sam about walking to school. Which question is right?
practice.explanation: After Did you, use the base verb walk without -ed.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I studied at the library yesterday.
practice.answer: I studied at the library yesterday.
options: I studied at the library yesterday.
I walked to the library yesterday.
I helped at the library yesterday.
practice.explanation: I studied means you read and learned at the library.

practice.prompt: Match the actions with the places or people.
practice.explanation: Studied fits school, helped fits your mother, and walked fits the park.

practice.prompt: Lily worked in the kitchen for her father. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I ___ my father in the kitchen.
practice.explanation: Use helped when you do something for someone.

practice.prompt: Ask Sam if he studied last night. Complete the question.
practice.explanation: Use Did you before the base verb study.

practice.prompt: Say that you walked home yesterday. Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use I walked home to say you went home on foot.

practice.prompt: Ask Lily if she helped her mother. Build the question.
practice.explanation: Use Did you + base verb help.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: I studied and I helped my parents.
practice.answer: I studied and I helped my parents.
practice.explanation: Both studied and helped are past verbs.

lessons.title: Yesterday with Smarty
lessons.scenario: Unit test in Smarty's playroom: wrap up Unit 10 and tell Smarty all about yesterday and last weekend.

items.note: Ask ‘What did you do?’ to find out someone's past actions.

items.example: I visited my parents last weekend.
items.note: Say ‘last weekend’ for the Saturday and Sunday before now.

items.example: I did not go to school last weekend.
items.note: Use ‘I did not’ plus a base verb, like ‘go’, to say what you did not do.

grammar.title: What did you do? and I did not…
grammar.explanation: Ask What did you do? to ask about past activities. To say what you did not do, use did not + base verb (I did not go, I did not watch TV).
examples: What did you do last weekend?
I did not go to the park yesterday.

practice.prompt: Smarty wants to know your activities from last weekend. Which question does he ask?
practice.answer: What did you do last weekend?
options: What did you do last weekend?
Where were you do last weekend?
What did you went last weekend?
practice.explanation: Use What did you do…? to ask about past actions.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I did not go to school last weekend.
practice.answer: I did not go to school last weekend.
options: I did not go to school last weekend.
I went to school last weekend.
I did not go to the park last weekend.
practice.explanation: I did not go says that you stayed away from school.

practice.prompt: Match the questions and answers.

pairs.right: I played tennis and cooked dinner.
No, I did not go to school.

practice.explanation: Match Where with a place, What did you do with actions, Did you go with did not go, and Was it with weather.

practice.prompt: You stayed home yesterday. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use I did not go (not went) for the negative past.

practice.prompt: Mia talks about Saturday and Sunday. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Last weekend means the Saturday and Sunday before now.

practice.prompt: Ask your friend what they did yesterday. Build the question.
practice.explanation: Start with What did you do, then add yesterday.

practice.prompt: Say that you bought a cake and met your friend last weekend. Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I bought a cake and met my friend last weekend.
practice.explanation: Combine bought and met with last weekend.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: I did not go to the park, I watched TV.
practice.answer: I did not go to the park, I watched TV.
practice.explanation: Say the whole sentence: I did not go to the park, I watched TV.

questions.prompt: What did Zara buy last weekend?

episode.title: The Yellow Key in the Playroom

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Last night I was in this room. My new red hat was on the table.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat points at an empty wooden table in his cozy playroom.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: Where is the red hat now? It is not on the table!

panels.speaker: Ben
panels.text: Yes, I came here yesterday. We played a game, and I went home.

image.describe: Ben the cat explains to Sam and Smarty in the playroom while pointing toward the door.

panels.speaker: Lily
panels.text: The window! I saw a small brown bird outside!

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Did the bird come in here?

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: There is a small yellow key under the window, next to the box!

image.describe: Mia the cat kneels beside a toy box under the playroom window, spotting a shiny yellow key.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: A yellow key! Whose is this? Let's go outside!
